sonnet.problem: The wrong answers "rest" and "move" are not believable ways to finish "refused to ___" after being disciplined. They are also much plainer than "repent", so the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

sonnet.problem: Verse 4 says only "Then I said". Nothing in the passage or its title names the speaker, but the card says "Jeremiah says".
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: The card names Jeremiah as the speaker of verse 5, which the passage does not name. It also asks "Who does he go to next?" as if he went, but the text only has the speaker say "I will go to the powerful".
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: Verse 7 says "Your children have forsaken Me". The card turns this into "His people have forsaken Him", which settles who "children" means. Cards 14 and 15 repeat the same change ("The LORD's people", "His people's needs").
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The text never says whether the search found anyone. The card claims "The LORD's questions show" the search result, which is an inference, and it cites verses 7 and 9, which do not state the answer.
sonnet.rule: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

sonnet.problem: The card calls Israel "the northern kingdom" and Judah "the southern kingdom". 1 Kings 12:19-21 does not use those labels. It also treats the "house of Israel" in verse 11 as only the northern kingdom, which the verse leaves open.
sonnet.rule: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.
